note: Section 4.4.1: "Since the SPD-I is just a part of the SPD, if a packet that is looked up in the SPD-I cannot be matched to an entry there, then the packet MUST be discarded." Re-judged 2026-11-12 (independent auditor) because apply.go::applyConfig changed: the one hunk adds warnICMPOverlapAtStart(cfg, s.log) beside warnImplicitDiscardAtStart in the applyStartup branch and widens its comment. warnICMPOverlapAtStart (icmp_overlap.go) only logs, at Error level, each refusal icmpOverlapRefusals answers; that function and refuseICMPErrorBypass / refuseICMPCheckDiscard read cfg (sorted map keys, per-entry copies) and write nothing, no SPD entry, no SA, no state field, and the call sits after the node catch-all, the application override guard, the IKE bypass, the interface entries and the prune, with no new return path. So the order the {gap} relies on holds over the current code: on the first apply installUnmatched goes in first, then applyApplicationOverride, then installIKEBypass; on a reload the guard and installXFRMInterfaceEntries run ahead of every SPD change; an interface catch-all refusal returns interfaceErr after the prune; releaseSPD still removes the catch-all last and keeps it when warnSPDLeft reports a leftover. Every other cited producer (vppPolicyInterface, releaseSPD, shutdown, warnSPDLeft, installUnmatched, verifyUnmatchedEnforceable, installXFRMInterfaceEntries, defaultDataplaneSource) is byte-identical to the previous judgement, as ./le rfc check names applyConfig alone. The two gap paths stand: VPP holds no entry bound to no interface and installs no catch-all (unmatched bypass only), and the OSPFv3 RFC 4552 manual-key entries have no final DISCARD entry beneath them with no vpn ipsec block, after releaseSPD, under unmatched bypass and on VPP; on either path an inbound packet matching no entry is delivered. Unimplemented stands; {gap} annotation accurate. The new start warning does not bear on this requirement: the configuration it warns about (a bypass entry or the bypass catch-all carrying ICMP errors beside an icmp-error-check peer, or an inbound discard entry the kernel's ICMP path overrides) concerns protected ICMP the kernel maps into or accepts from a Child SA, not a clear packet that meets no SPD-I entry.
